# A creator-dispatch block means "invoke the creator skill", not "retry the write"

## What happened

While building PR156, AI's `Write` / `Edit` on `SKILL.md`, a `.claude/rules/` file, `.py`,
`.yaml`, and `CLAUDE.md` triggered `creator-dispatch` `PreToolUse` blocks. These are
**session-flag blocks** (they `decision: block` the first matching edit, then pass subsequent
edits in the same session). AI treated each block as a one-time gate and **immediately retried
the same Write**, hand-authoring the `SKILL.md` and a generator script. The user had to
explicitly say "スキル作るときは /skill-creator つかえ" and "/py-script これ使って" to redirect.

## Why it matters

The dispatch block exists to route creation through the proper creator skill (`skill-creator`,
`rule-creator`, `claude-creator`, `dev-kit:py-script` / `py-project`), which enforces step
structure, JP mirrors, and provenance stamps. Retrying the raw write skips all of that — the
hand-written `SKILL.md` later needed its provenance stamp corrected, and the script had to be
reworked to `py-script` conventions and then deleted entirely.

## Lesson

When a `creator-dispatch` `PreToolUse` block fires, **invoke the named creator skill** rather
than retrying the edit. The session-flag pass-through is meant for the edits you make *after*
going through the creator skill — it is not a license to bypass it on the second attempt.
